notes: LightBench's downloadable AI models (docs/PHASE3.md Part 24). The files are NOT in git: the deploy workflow fetches each pinned file by exact URL (source.repo at source.revision) and checks its byte count and SHA-256 (web/scripts/models.mjs fetch), failing the build on any mismatch, then serves it from LightBench's own GitHub Pages site under models/<id>/<revision 7>/<variant>.onnx.

While source.revision or a file's sha256 is null the model is not pinned: the workflow skips it with a warning and the app says the model isn't available in that build. Pin it on a machine that can reach huggingface.co with `node web/scripts/models.mjs pin` (it reads the Hugging Face commit, the Git LFS pointers' sha256 and size, downloads each file and checks it against them, and writes this file).

bytes: as read from the Git LFS pointers of the repository's main branch on 2026-10-13 (docs/research/cowork-2026-10-13b/F_MODEL_DELIVERY.md, F3); `pin` replaces them with the pinned revision's values.

Moebius (AI Remove) is delivered from Hugging Face ("delivery": "huggingface", owner's decision 2026-10-21): at about 1.24 GB it is too big for GitHub Pages' 1 GB site limit, so the deploy skips it and the app downloads the three files itself, after the user agrees, from the commit-pinned /resolve/ URLs, checking each file's size and SHA-256. Pinned by the owner's decision, not by `models.mjs pin` (which leaves it alone). docs/PHASE3.md Part 26.

Schema 2 (docs/PHASE3.md Part 27): a model may be several graphs ("part"), each graph's weights in its own file beside it ("data": true, ONNX external data), served from the site under their own file names (models/<id>/<revision 7>/<file name>). SAM 2.1 Hiera Tiny (Object select) is pinned by the owner's decision from the checked run in MASKS_PREP.md (GitHub Actions run 39653265084: every file's size and SHA-256 matched its Git LFS pointer); `models.mjs pin` leaves it alone ("pinnedBy": "owner").

LightBench's own conversions (docs/PHASE3.md Part 29): the Sky model's authors publish PyTorch weights only, so the "AI models" workflow's efficientvit-export task exports them to ONNX on GitHub's runner from the pinned checkpoint ("convertedFrom"), checks the export against the authors' PyTorch model and publishes it, with its licence and a SOURCE note, as an asset of a GitHub Release of this repository ("host": "github-release", the release's "tag", and the commit the tag points at as "revision"). A release is never overwritten: a new export gets a new tag. The deploy fetches the asset from the release and checks its size and SHA-256 like the others; `models.mjs pin` leaves it alone.

People and faces (docs/PHASE3.md Part 28): RF-DETR-Seg Nano is delivered from Hugging Face by the app ("delivery": "huggingface", owner's decision 2026-10-21); YuNet (from GitHub, opencv/opencv_zoo, a Git LFS file: the deploy fetches it from media.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit) and MediaPipe Selfie Multiclass (the community ONNX conversion) are served from LightBench's own site. All three are pinned by the owner's decision from the checked run in MASKS_PREP.md (GitHub Actions run 39653265084: each file's size and SHA-256 matched its Git LFS pointer).

Subject (docs/PHASE3.md Part 30): BiRefNet_lite as onnx-community converted it can't run in a browser with ONNX Runtime Web 1.30.0 (too many buffers per WebGPU kernel; up to 4.4 GiB of activations on the processor, over WebAssembly's 4 GiB). The "AI models" workflow's birefnet-patch task downloads the pinned onnx-community file ("convertedFrom.weights", checked by size and SHA-256), rearranges its graph without changing its weights (web/scripts/subject/birefnet_patch.py), checks it against the original on the CPU, and against the fp32 original ("convertedFrom.reference"), runs the app's own Subject code on it, and publishes it with its licence and a SOURCE note as a GitHub Release of this repository ("host": "github-release"), never overwriting one. The deploy fetches it from the release like the Sky model.

models.name: Depth Anything V2 Small
models.summary: Estimates how near or far each part of a photo is (relative depth), for the Depth range mask.

licence.statement: “Depth-Anything-V2-Small model is under the Apache-2.0 license. Depth-Anything-V2-Base/Large/Giant models are under the CC-BY-NC-4.0 license.” (Depth Anything V2 README, commit a561b84)

models.credit: Lihe Yang, Bingyi Kang, Zilong Huang, Zhen Zhao, Xiaogang Xu, Jiashi Feng and Hengshuang Zhao: “Depth Anything V2” (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2406.09414). Code and weights: github.com/DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2. ONNX export: Hugging Face onnx-community.
models.trainingData: The model was trained on 595K synthetic images (BlendedMVS, Hypersim, IRS, TartanAir, Virtual KITTI 2) and about 62M real photos labelled by a larger model (BDD100K, Google Landmarks, ImageNet-21K, LSUN, Objects365, Open Images V7, Places365, SA-1B), as listed in the paper’s Table 7. These training sets are named publicly; some of them have non-commercial or research-only terms, for example SA-1B and Virtual KITTI 2. The model’s own licence is Apache-2.0.

models.name: Moebius
models.summary: Fills in what you paint over with the AI Remove brush: it draws new detail that continues the surroundings, so objects disappear instead of being patched from elsewhere in the photo.

licence.statement: “Both the code and the pretrained model weights of Moebius are released under the Apache License 2.0” and “Commercial use of the weights and the images produced with them is permitted.” (Moebius README on GitHub, commit b88d462, 2026-08-12)
licence.notes: The Hugging Face page of the original weights (hustvl/Moebius) is tagged MIT and has no licence file; LightBench relies on the Apache-2.0 statement in the authors’ GitHub repository. The part that turns pictures into the model’s working form and back (its VAE) comes from the same authors’ earlier PixelHacker, which uses Stability AI’s SDXL VAE; PixelHacker’s Hugging Face copy is tagged MIT, with no licence file or copyright line. The files LightBench downloads are Simon Willison’s ONNX conversion (simonw/Moebius-ONNX, Apache-2.0).

models.credit: Kangsheng Duan, Ziyang Xu, Wenyu Liu, Xiaohu Ruan, Xiaoxin Chen and Xinggang Wang (Huazhong University of Science and Technology and vivo AI Lab): “Moebius: 0.2B Lightweight Image Inpainting Framework with 10B-Level Performance” (ECCV 2026, arXiv:2606.19195). Code and weights: github.com/hustvl/Moebius. VAE: hustvl/PixelHacker. ONNX conversion: Simon Willison (huggingface.co/simonw/Moebius-ONNX).
models.trainingData: Moebius was trained to imitate its authors’ earlier, larger model, PixelHacker, and this version was then fine-tuned on Places2 (photos of places). PixelHacker was trained on 14 million images with masks from COCONut-Large, Objects365 V2, Google Landmarks V2 and a collection of 7.49 million natural-scene photos that its authors gathered and have not named (about half of the images), then fine-tuned on Places2, CelebA-HQ and FFHQ. Which images were used to train Moebius from PixelHacker isn’t stated. So not all of its training data is named publicly: LightBench’s owner accepted this as an exception to the rule that a model’s training data must be named. Some of the named sets carry non-commercial or research-only terms, for example FFHQ.

checkpoint.name: ft_places2
checkpoint.source: export script, not model card (simonw/moebius-web python/reexport_unet_no_conv3d.py at 080be6e)

models.name: SAM 2.1 Hiera Tiny
models.summary: Finds the object you point at, for Object select: it outlines what is under the pointer, and a click makes it a mask.

licence.statement: “The SAM 2 model checkpoints, SAM 2 demo code (front-end and back-end), and SAM 2 training code are licensed under Apache 2.0” (SAM 2 README on GitHub, commit 2b90b9f)
licence.notes: The ONNX conversion LightBench uses (onnx-community/sam2.1-hiera-tiny-ONNX on Hugging Face) has no licence tag or licence file of its own; LightBench relies on Meta’s Apache-2.0 statement for the weights it was converted from.

models.credit: Nikhila Ravi, Valentin Gabeur, Yuan-Ting Hu, Ronghang Hu, Chaitanya Ryali, Tengyu Ma, Haitham Khedr, Roman Rädle, Chloe Rolland, Laura Gustafson, Eric Mintun, Junting Pan, Kalyan Vasudev Alwala, Nicolas Carion, Chao-Yuan Wu, Ross Girshick, Piotr Dollár and Christoph Feichtenhofer (Meta FAIR): “SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos” (arXiv:2408.00714). Code and weights (SAM 2.1): github.com/facebookresearch/sam2. ONNX export: Hugging Face onnx-community.
models.trainingData: SAM 2 was trained on photos and videos with outlined objects: SA-1B (11 million photos, published by Meta for research use only), SA-V (videos published by Meta under the CC BY 4.0 licence) and about 15 % of Meta’s own licensed videos, which are not published (the paper gives the mix as about 15 % SA-1B, 70 % SA-V and 15 % Meta’s videos). So not all of its training data is published: LightBench’s owner accepted this under the rule that a small unpublished share may be used if it is stated plainly. The model’s own licence is Apache-2.0.

models.name: EfficientViT-Seg B1 (ADE20K)
models.summary: Finds the sky in a photo, for the Sky mask: it sorts each part of the photo into one of 150 kinds of thing (sky, tree, building, person and so on), and LightBench keeps the parts it calls sky.

licence.statement: The weights’ Hugging Face page (han-cai/efficientvit-seg, commit cf3ccaf) is tagged “apache-2.0”, and the authors’ code repository (mit-han-lab/efficientvit, commit de7d773) is under the Apache License 2.0 (“Copyright [2023] [Han Cai]”).
licence.notes: The file LightBench downloads is LightBench’s own ONNX conversion of the authors’ efficientvit_seg_b1_ade20k.pt weights: made and checked against the authors’ PyTorch model by LightBench’s “AI models” workflow, and published with this licence and a note of where it came from as a release of LightBench’s own repository on GitHub.

models.credit: Han Cai, Junyan Li, Muyan Hu, Chuang Gan and Song Han (MIT Han Lab): “EfficientViT: Lightweight Multi-Scale Attention for High-Resolution Dense Prediction” (ICCV 2023, arXiv:2205.14756). Code: github.com/mit-han-lab/efficientvit. Weights: huggingface.co/han-cai/efficientvit-seg. ONNX conversion: LightBench.
models.trainingData: The model learnt to sort the parts of a photo on ADE20K: about 20,000 photos of everyday scenes, each outlined by hand into 150 kinds of thing, sky among them, published by MIT. ADE20K’s terms allow its use for non-commercial research and education only. The part of the model that first reads the photo was trained before that on ImageNet-1K (about 1.28 million photos sorted into 1,000 categories), whose terms likewise allow non-commercial research and education only. Both sets are named publicly. The model’s own licence is Apache-2.0.

models.name: RF-DETR-Seg Nano
models.summary: Finds the people in a photo and outlines each one, for People masks.

licence.statement: “The open-source `rfdetr` package and Apache-designated model weights are licensed under Apache License 2.0”, and RF-DETR-Seg-N is listed with the licence “Apache 2.0” (RF-DETR README on GitHub, develop branch, read 2026-10-26).
licence.notes: The files LightBench downloads are a community ONNX conversion (PierreMarieCurie/rf-detr-onnx on Hugging Face, tagged Apache-2.0); Roboflow publishes no ONNX file of this model itself.

models.credit: Isaac Robinson, Peter Robicheaux, Matvei Popov, Deva Ramanan and Neehar Peri (Roboflow): “RF-DETR: Real-Time Detection Transformer” (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2511.09554). Code and weights: github.com/roboflow/rf-detr. ONNX conversion: Pierre-Marie Curie (huggingface.co/PierreMarieCurie/rf-detr-onnx).
models.trainingData: The model was trained on COCO (photos from Flickr with outlines published under CC BY 4.0; the photos keep Flickr’s terms) after pre-training on Objects365 (published for academic use only). Its pre-training outlines were made by Meta’s SAM 2, which was itself trained partly on Meta’s own videos that are not published, and its backbone (DINOv2) was trained by Meta on LVD-142M, a collection of web images that is not published. So not all of the data behind it is published: LightBench’s owner accepted this under the rule that unpublished foundation data may be used if it is stated plainly. The model’s own licence is Apache-2.0.

models.name: YuNet
models.summary: Finds faces in a photo, so People masks know which face belongs to whom.

licence.statement: “All files in this directory are licensed under MIT License.” (OpenCV Zoo, models/face_detection_yunet/README.md, commit 48b10fa)

models.credit: Wei Wu, Hanyang Peng and Shiqi Yu: “YuNet: A Tiny Millisecond-level Face Detector” (Machine Intelligence Research, 2023). Training code: github.com/ShiqiYu/libfacedetection.train. ONNX file: OpenCV Zoo (github.com/opencv/opencv_zoo).
models.trainingData: The model was trained on WIDER FACE (photos of crowds and events gathered from the web, published under the Creative Commons licence “cc by-nc-nd”: non-commercial use, no derivatives). The training set is named publicly; its own terms are non-commercial. The model’s own licence is MIT.

models.name: MediaPipe Selfie Multiclass
models.summary: Tells a person’s hair, face skin, body skin and clothes apart, for People masks.

licence.statement: “Licensed under: Apache License, Version 2.0” (Google’s model card, “Model Card Multiclass Segmentation”).
licence.notes: Google publishes this model for its MediaPipe library only (as a TFLite file). The file LightBench uses is a community ONNX conversion (FreeHugsForRobots/ps-skin-seg on Hugging Face, tagged Apache-2.0), checked against Google’s own file: the same answers on a test photo.

models.credit: Google: MediaPipe Selfie Multiclass Segmentation (MediaPipe Image Segmenter, github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe). ONNX conversion: FreeHugsForRobots (huggingface.co/FreeHugsForRobots/ps-skin-seg).
models.trainingData: Google doesn’t name the data this model was trained on: its model card says only that it was “trained on thousands of samples with diverse identities”. LightBench’s rule is that a model’s training data must be named; LightBench’s owner approved this model as an exception (a well-known publisher that names no data).

models.name: BiRefNet_lite
models.summary: Finds the main subject of a photo (the person, animal or thing the photo is about), for the Subject mask: it gives each pixel how much it belongs to the subject, so hair, fur and fine edges stay soft.

licence.statement: The authors’ code repository (ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet, commit f707963) is under the MIT License (“Copyright (c) 2024 ZhengPeng”), the weights’ Hugging Face page (ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet_lite) is tagged “mit”, and so is the ONNX conversion’s (onnx-community/BiRefNet_lite-ONNX, commit de15b22).
licence.notes: The file LightBench downloads is LightBench’s own copy of onnx-community’s conversion, its graph arranged so that it runs in a browser with the weights unchanged, checked against the original by LightBench’s “AI models” workflow and published with this licence and a note of where it came from as a release of LightBench’s own repository on GitHub.

models.credit: Peng Zheng, Dehong Gao, Deng-Ping Fan, Li Liu, Jorma Laaksonen, Wanli Ouyang and Nicu Sebe: “Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation” (CAAI Artificial Intelligence Research, 2024; arXiv:2401.03407). Code and weights: github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet. ONNX conversion: onnx-community on Hugging Face. Arranged for browsers: LightBench.
models.trainingData: The authors give two different lists, and they disagree. The model table in the authors’ code repository on GitHub says this model learnt from DIS5K, DUTS, HRSOD, UHRSD, HRS10K, P3M-10k and TR-humans: published sets of photos in which people outlined the main subject by hand (TR-humans is made of computer-generated people). The model’s Hugging Face page says it learnt from DIS5K’s training photos only. Either way DIS5K is among them, and DIS5K’s terms allow non-commercial research and education only. Of the others, DUTS says “all rights reserved” without terms for other uses, HRSOD gives no terms, UHRSD and HRS10K come with MIT-licensed code without saying whether that covers the photos, P3M-10k is released under the MIT licence for research, and TR-humans under Apache-2.0. The part of the model that first reads the photo (a Swin Transformer) started from Microsoft’s weights trained on ImageNet-22K and ImageNet-1K, whose terms allow non-commercial research and education only. All these sets are named publicly. The model’s own licence is MIT.
